themes.thesis: Capex supercycle still compounding; the bottleneck the whole AI economy pays a toll to.
Electricity is the binding constraint on AI. Multi-decade buildout, but 2026 prices already discount a lot.
Structural rearmament plus a genuine software/autonomy displacement of primes.
Storage attach rates and supply-chain onshoring are policy-supported and accelerating.
Stablecoin rails are a real threat to card economics — this theme has a genuine short side.
The next frontier after language models, but revenue is still mostly ahead of the narrative.
Obesity franchise economics are extraordinary; AI-discovery pure plays remain unproven.
Launch cost collapse is real; direct-to-device is the swing factor. High dispersion, high beta.
Biggest winners are the hyperscalers; seat-based SaaS faces the clearest AI business-model risk.
Non-discretionary spend, but AI is compressing seat-based pricing and inviting autonomous-agent entrants.

privates.name: OpenAI
privates.description: Leading AI lab (ChatGPT, GPT models) whose massive compute purchasing and custom silicon ambitions reshape chip demand
privates.threat: OpenAI's push for custom inference silicon (with Broadcom) and alternative chip suppliers (Cerebras, AMD) threatens to diversify demand away from pure Nvidia dependence while its scale validates the entire AI-chip buildout.

privates.name: Anthropic
privates.description: AI safety-focused lab (Claude models) with massive multi-cloud compute commitments across chip vendors
privates.threat: Anthropic's diversified compute strategy across AWS Trainium, Google TPUs, and Nvidia GPUs pressures Nvidia's pricing power and validates alternative accelerator architectures at hyperscale.

privates.name: xAI
privates.description: Elon Musk's AI lab (Grok models) building some of the world's largest GPU clusters (Colossus)
privates.threat: xAI's rapid buildout of the largest GPU clusters in the world is one of Nvidia's single biggest demand drivers, while its interest in alternative silicon signals future diversification risk.

privates.name: Cerebras Systems
privates.description: Maker of wafer-scale AI chips (WSE-3) for ultra-fast inference, now publicly traded after May 2026 IPO
privates.threat: Cerebras's wafer-scale architecture beat Nvidia on single-user inference speed and landed a $10B OpenAI compute deal, proving non-GPU inference architectures can win at hyperscale before Cerebras itself went public.

privates.name: Groq
privates.description: Inference-chip pioneer (LPU) pivoting to an inference-cloud operator after licensing its core IP to Nvidia
privates.threat: Nvidia's reported $20B non-exclusive licensing deal for Groq's LPU technology both validates fast-inference architecture as a real threat and shows Nvidia absorbing rather than losing to non-GPU challengers.

privates.name: SambaNova Systems
privates.description: AI chipmaker (SN40L/SN50) focused on inference chips and on-premise enterprise AI deployments
privates.threat: SambaNova's on-premise inference chips and near-acquisition talks with Intel highlight both real enterprise demand for Nvidia alternatives and the difficulty of independently scaling against Nvidia's ecosystem lock-in.

privates.name: Tenstorrent
privates.description: Jim Keller-led AI chip designer building discrete, workstation-scale AI accelerators, reportedly in acquisition talks with Qualcomm
privates.last_round: Reported $8-10B acquisition talks with Qualcomm, Jul 2026 (prior: sought $3.2B valuation round, Nov 2025)
privates.threat: Qualcomm's reported bid for Tenstorrent at up to $10B signals large semiconductor incumbents see standalone AI-chip IP as strategically necessary, validating the broader non-Nvidia accelerator thesis.

privates.name: Etched
privates.description: Builder of transformer-specific ASICs (Sohu chip) designed exclusively to accelerate transformer-model inference
privates.threat: Etched's bet that a transformer-only ASIC can dramatically outperform general-purpose GPUs on cost-per-token is a direct wager against Nvidia's flexible-architecture moat.

privates.name: Fermi America
privates.description: Developer of the world's largest private, behind-the-meter nuclear-and-gas power grid and AI data-center campus in Texas
privates.threat: Fermi's plan to build a private, off-grid multi-gigawatt power campus (nuclear, gas, solar, storage) competing directly for hyperscaler tenants threatens to disintermediate incumbent regulated utilities and IPPs from AI power contracts.

privates.name: Valar Atomics
privates.description: Developer of standardized, mass-manufactured waterless small modular nuclear reactors for AI data centers
privates.threat: Valar's factory-built waterless reactors, already powering an Nvidia Blackwell cluster in partnership with Nvidia, threaten to undercut incumbent generators on speed-to-power for AI campuses.

privates.name: Blue Energy Global
privates.description: Startup building grid-scale nuclear reactors constructed in shipyards to cut cost and schedule for data-center power
privates.threat: Blue Energy's shipyard-manufacturing model for 1.5GW reactors targets the same speed-to-power gap that has driven utilities and IPPs to underbuild for AI demand, offering a faster alternative supply route.

privates.name: Antares Nuclear
privates.description: Small modular reactor developer targeting U.S. military bases and price-insensitive critical infrastructure customers
privates.threat: Antares's Pentagon-backed SMR contracts show private nuclear capital increasingly bypassing traditional utility procurement, creating an alternative power-supply track for critical AI and defense loads.

privates.name: Crusoe Energy
privates.description: Vertically integrated 'AI factory' company combining rapid energy sourcing, data-center construction, and cloud services (developer behind Stargate Abilene)
privates.last_round: $1.375B Series E (equity, Oct 2025) plus $11.6B debt/equity phase-two (May 2026)
privates.total_raised: $3B+ equity, plus tens of billions in project debt
privates.threat: Crusoe's model of bundling power sourcing with data-center construction lets hyperscalers skip traditional utility interconnection queues, threatening to route gigawatts of new demand around incumbent grid operators and IPPs.

privates.name: CoreWeave
privates.description: GPU-cloud operator whose massive power procurement and financing structures underpin the AI-infrastructure debt market (note: now publicly traded, included for power-market relevance)
privates.stage: publicly traded (IPO Mar 2025), power/financing model still disrupting sector
privates.threat: CoreWeave's GPU-backed, investment-grade financing structure lets it lock up 1.7GW of active power capacity via bankruptcy-remote SPVs, a template competitors and IPPs must now match to win hyperscaler leases.

privates.name: Vantage Data Centers
privates.description: Private data-center developer building multi-gigawatt AI campuses (Stargate Frontier, Lighthouse) financed via infrastructure debt
privates.last_round: $25B Frontier campus commitment, 2026 (project financing, not corporate equity round)
privates.total_raised: tens of billions in project-level debt and equity since 2020
privates.threat: Vantage's ability to finance and deliver 1,000+ MW campuses within a single year outpaces the buildout cadence of regulated utilities, forcing incumbents to accelerate capacity additions or lose hyperscaler tenants.

privates.name: TerraPower
privates.description: Bill Gates-backed developer of next-generation Natrium sodium-fast nuclear reactors for industrial and tech customers
privates.last_round: Undisclosed growth funding, ongoing (DOE-backed demonstration project in Wyoming)
privates.threat: TerraPower's advanced Natrium reactor, backed by Amazon and Bill Gates, positions next-gen nuclear as a long-horizon threat to gas-peaker and traditional nuclear operators competing for AI baseload contracts.

privates.name: Anduril Industries
privates.description: Vertically integrated defense company building autonomous drones, munitions, and software (Lattice OS) for the US military and allies
privates.threat: Anduril's software-defined, mass-manufactured autonomy platforms directly threaten legacy primes' cost-plus hardware model while validating investor appetite for defense disruption at massive scale.

privates.name: Shield AI
privates.description: Maker of Hivemind autonomy software and X-Bat autonomous aircraft for contested-environment drone operations
privates.threat: Selection for the US Air Force Collaborative Combat Aircraft program shows autonomy software startups can win prime roles on next-gen fighter drone programs traditionally reserved for LMT/RTX.

privates.name: Saronic Technologies
privates.description: Builder of autonomous surface vessels (Marauder-class) for naval defense and maritime autonomy at scale
privates.threat: Saronic's rapid unmanned-vessel production (targeting 20+ ships/year) directly challenges traditional shipbuilders and primes for Navy uncrewed surface vessel programs at a fraction of legacy cost and schedule.

privates.name: Helsing
privates.description: Munich-based European defense AI company building software for drones, aircraft, and submarines for NATO militaries
privates.threat: As Europe's largest defense startup pushing 'sovereign AI,' Helsing threatens US primes' access to European rearmament budgets and validates AI-native defense software as a category outside the US market.

privates.name: Epirus
privates.description: Maker of Leonidas high-power microwave counter-drone directed-energy weapon systems
privates.threat: Epirus' directed-energy counter-swarm systems offer a cheaper, scalable alternative to missile-based air defense sold by RTX and LMT, addressing the drone-saturation threat exposed in recent conflicts.

privates.name: Castelion
privates.description: SpaceX-alumni-founded startup mass-producing low-cost hypersonic strike weapons (Blackbeard)
privates.threat: Castelion's commercial-style rapid iteration on hypersonic munitions challenges LMT/RTX's historic monopoly on hypersonic weapons development and could undercut their unit economics on future contracts.

privates.name: Applied Intuition
privates.description: Vehicle intelligence/simulation software company expanding into defense autonomy (Axion, Acuity) via EpiSci acquisition
privates.threat: Applied Intuition's push from autonomous-vehicle simulation into defense autonomy software threatens to displace prime-built mission software and simulation environments used across LMT/RTX programs.

privates.name: Skydio
privates.description: US-made autonomous drone manufacturer serving enterprise, public safety, and defense customers, positioned against DJI
privates.threat: Skydio's domestic manufacturing scale and regulatory tailwinds from Chinese-drone bans directly erode AeroVironment's small-drone market share in public safety and defense.

privates.name: SpaceX
privates.description: Dominant launch, Starlink satellite broadband, and Starship deep-space company preparing for a landmark IPO
privates.threat: SpaceX's Starlink and Starship dominance dwarfs every public space comp combined, and its pending IPO (targeting up to $800B+ valuation) will reset the entire sector's valuation benchmarks overnight.

privates.name: Stoke Space
privates.description: Developer of the fully and rapidly reusable Nova medium-lift launch vehicle at Cape Canaveral
privates.last_round: $860M Series D, Feb 2026 (in process of raising ~$1B further, Aug 2026)
privates.threat: Stoke's fully reusable Nova rocket, backed by a rising ~$9B valuation, directly targets Rocket Lab's and legacy primes' medium-lift launch market with a SpaceX-style reusability model.

privates.name: K2 Space
privates.description: Manufacturer of large, high-power satellite buses for commercial and defense constellations
privates.threat: K2's high-power large-satellite platforms compete directly with Iridium's and AST SpaceMobile's next-gen constellation hardware, and its rapid production model threatens legacy satellite bus suppliers.

privates.name: True Anomaly
privates.description: Builder of autonomous spacecraft and space-based interceptors for space domain awareness and Golden Dome missile defense
privates.threat: True Anomaly's space-interceptor role in the Golden Dome missile-defense program positions it to capture national security space budgets that would otherwise flow to Boeing and legacy space-defense primes.

privates.name: Impulse Space
privates.description: Builder of orbital transfer vehicles ('space tugs') for in-space mobility, founded by SpaceX propulsion veteran Tom Mueller
privates.threat: Impulse Space's orbital mobility infrastructure threatens to become the default 'last mile' layer for satellite deployment, disintermediating launch providers like Rocket Lab from higher-margin orbit-raising services.

privates.name: Apex Space
privates.description: Mass-manufacturer of productized, configurable satellite bus platforms (Aries, Nova, Comet) for commercial and defense payloads
privates.threat: Apex's high-rate, standardized satellite bus production model undercuts custom-built satellite platforms, threatening incumbent suppliers' margins as Pentagon demand for rapid constellation deployment grows.

privates.name: Varda Space Industries
privates.description: Operator of reentry capsules for microgravity manufacturing (pharmaceuticals) and hypersonics testing
privates.threat: Varda's reentry-capsule and in-space manufacturing niche opens a new commercial space revenue category (pharma manufacturing, hypersonics testing) that diversifies demand beyond launch, indirectly pressuring Rocket Lab's reentry ambitions.

privates.name: Axiom Space
privates.description: Developer of commercial space station (Axiom Station) and NASA spacesuits (AxEMU) as ISS successor
privates.threat: Axiom's role as the leading ISS-successor commercial station builder directly challenges Boeing's legacy human-spaceflight infrastructure position as NASA transitions off the ISS by 2030.

privates.name: Figure AI
privates.description: Developer of general-purpose humanoid robots (Figure 03) for logistics, manufacturing and eventually home use
privates.threat: At a $39B valuation and backed by Nvidia and Brookfield, Figure directly threatens to leapfrog traditional industrial automation and warehouse robotics incumbents with general-purpose humanoids.

privates.name: Physical Intelligence
privates.description: Builds general-purpose AI foundation models ('robot brains') that can control many different robot bodies
privates.last_round: $600M, Nov 2025 (in talks for ~$1B more at >$11B, Mar 2026)
privates.threat: Its foundation-model 'brain' approach could commoditize the control software layer that industrial automation vendors like Rockwell and Fanuc currently bundle with their hardware.

privates.name: Skild AI
privates.description: Builds an 'omni-bodied' foundation model (Skild Brain) designed to operate any robot for any task across industrial and commercial settings
privates.threat: Skild's revenue-generating omni-bodied brain, already deployed in warehouses, manufacturing and data centers, threatens to displace proprietary robot-control software sold by industrial automation incumbents.

privates.name: Apptronik
privates.description: Austin-based maker of the Apollo humanoid robot for factories, warehouses and logistics, partnered with Google DeepMind
privates.threat: Apollo is already piloting in Mercedes-Benz and GXO Logistics facilities, positioning Apptronik to beat Tesla Optimus and Chinese humanoids to commercial warehouse/factory deployment ahead of incumbents like Rockwell and Symbotic.

privates.name: 1X Technologies
privates.description: Norwegian, OpenAI-backed maker of the NEO bipedal humanoid robot targeting home and enterprise (logistics, guarding) use
privates.threat: 1X's consumer-home NEO strategy, backed directly by OpenAI, opens an entirely new physical-AI market beyond industrial floors that none of the public comps currently address.

privates.name: Agility Robotics
privates.description: Maker of the Digit bipedal warehouse/logistics humanoid robot, going public via SPAC merger with Churchill Capital Corp XI
privates.threat: As the first pure-play humanoid robotics company to go public, Agility validates warehouse-humanoid economics deployed at Amazon, Toyota and GXO sites, directly threatening Symbotic and Zebra's warehouse automation stacks.

privates.name: Neura Robotics
privates.description: German full-stack cognitive robotics company building humanoid (4NE1) and industrial robots plus the Neuraverse shared-intelligence platform
privates.threat: Backed by major tech and industrial investors, Neura is Europe's best-funded physical-AI challenger to Fanuc- and Rockwell-style industrial automation incumbents.

privates.name: Unitree Robotics
privates.description: Hangzhou-based maker of humanoid robots and quadruped robot dogs, mainland China's first listed humanoid-robot company
privates.total_raised: IPO plus prior VC rounds from Geely, Alibaba, Tencent
privates.threat: Unitree's profitable, low-cost humanoid production model and fresh public capital threaten to undercut Western and Japanese robotics incumbents on price at scale.

privates.name: XBOW
privates.description: Autonomous offensive security platform that uses AI to discover and validate software vulnerabilities at scale, replacing manual penetration testing.
privates.threat: Autonomous AI pentesting commoditizes a core revenue stream for traditional MDR/EDR vendors and reduces dependence on human red teams that CRWD and PANW rely on as high-margin services.

privates.name: Socket
privates.description: Software supply chain security platform that protects enterprises from malicious open-source dependencies introduced via AI-assisted coding.
privates.threat: Addresses the fastest-growing attack surface in enterprise security — AI-generated code pulling in unvetted open-source packages — where CRWD and ZS lack native depth.

privates.name: Torq
privates.description: Agentic AI security operations platform automating SOC workflows, alert triage, and incident response for multinational enterprises.
privates.threat: Agentic SOC automation threatens the professional-services and Cortex XSOAR revenues of PANW and the Singularity suite upsell economics of SentinelOne.

privates.name: Abnormal AI
privates.description: AI-native email and collaboration security platform using behavioral analysis to stop sophisticated phishing, BEC, and account-takeover attacks.
privates.threat: Behavioral AI email security erodes email gateway revenues at PANW and CRWD and competes directly with OKTA's identity-centric threat detection as BEC attacks evolve.

privates.name: Zafran Security
privates.description: AI-native threat exposure management platform that uses existing security tools to prove 90% of critical vulnerabilities are unexploitable and autonomously remediates the remaining 10%.
privates.threat: Directly challenges vulnerability management modules in PANW's Cortex and CRWD's Falcon by reducing remediation times from weeks to hours using AI-native exposure scoring.

privates.name: Zenity
privates.description: Cybersecurity platform that governs and secures autonomous AI agents across enterprise environments, preventing agent-level attacks and data exfiltration.
privates.threat: As enterprises deploy millions of AI agents, Zenity's AI-agent governance layer fills a gap that CRWD, OKTA, and ZS have not yet addressed natively, threatening to become the de facto control plane for agentic security.

privates.name: Eye Security
privates.description: European integrated cybersecurity platform combining AI-powered threat detection, 24/7 human SOC, incident response, and in-house cyber insurance for mid-market enterprises.
privates.threat: Challenges FTNT and PANW's European mid-market position by offering a sovereign, GDPR-compliant integrated stack — particularly relevant as NIS2 drives mandatory security spend.

privates.name: Isomorphic Labs
privates.description: Alphabet-spun AI drug design company using AlphaFold-derived models to design novel therapeutics across multiple modalities, with partnerships with Lilly, Novartis, and J&J.
privates.threat: If IsoDDE delivers clinical candidates at scale, Isomorphic becomes a platform layer that renders traditional CRO-based discovery at LLY and NVO obsolete and could capture royalties on drug programs at both companies.

privates.name: Chai Discovery
privates.description: AI molecular design company building foundation models that predict and reprogram molecular interactions for drug discovery, with pharma partnerships with Lilly, Pfizer, and Novartis.
privates.threat: Chai-3's double-digit experimental success rate in de novo antibody design directly erodes SDGR's computational chemistry and RXRX's phenomics edge while commoditizing early discovery for big pharma partners LLY and NVO.

privates.name: Xaira Therapeutics
privates.description: Integrated AI biotech using generative protein design and large biological models to discover next-generation therapeutics targeting hard-to-drug biology.
privates.threat: With the deepest capital base in AI-native drug discovery and Nobel laureate co-founder David Baker, Xaira threatens to bypass clinical-stage public biotechs like VRTX by generating first-in-class biologics that legacy platforms cannot reach.

privates.name: EvolutionaryScale
privates.description: AI protein language model company (ESM3) that generates novel proteins compressing millions of years of evolution, enabling therapeutic and industrial biotech applications.
privates.threat: ESM3's open and commercial protein generation platform challenges ILMN's sequencing-centric data moat and SDGR's structural biology software by making de novo protein design accessible and cheap.

privates.name: insitro
privates.description: AI drug discovery company founded by Daphne Koller building a data engine around human biology with partnerships with BMS (ALS), Gilead (NASH), and Lilly (metabolism).
privates.threat: insitro's Virtual Human platform competing on ALS, NASH, and metabolic targets with BMS and Lilly validation undermines the narrative that public TechBio companies like RXRX have a monopoly on AI-native discovery.

privates.name: Genesis Therapeutics
privates.description: AI-native drug discovery company focused on generative chemistry and translational biology to produce clinical-stage small molecules for undruggable targets.
privates.threat: Genesis's generative chemistry platform directly competes with SDGR's Maestro and RXRX's Recursion OS by targeting the same undruggable protein space, threatening to make SDGR's software licensing model irrelevant.

privates.name: Form Energy
privates.description: Long-duration iron-air battery company capable of 100-hour discharge, targeting multi-day grid storage to complement intermittent renewables and AI data center power needs.
privates.threat: Iron-air chemistry with 10x lower cost per kWh than lithium threatens FLNC's and EOSE's long-duration propositions and could undercut TSLA's Megapack pricing for utility-scale deployments.

privates.name: Redwood Materials
privates.description: Battery recycling and cathode production company founded by ex-Tesla CTO JB Straubel, now expanding into second-life EV battery energy storage for AI data centers.
privates.threat: Redwood's recycling-to-cathode loop threatens ALB and MP by creating a domestic circular supply chain that reduces dependence on virgin lithium and rare earth imports, potentially capping long-term lithium pricing power.

privates.name: Base Power
privates.description: Residential and commercial energy storage company offering a 39.2 kWh home battery (Core) with 36-hour backup, deploying as a virtual power plant network.
privates.threat: Base Power's $13B valuation and VPP network model directly challenges ENPH's IQ Battery dominance and TSLA's Powerwall by offering longer backup duration and a utility-facing fleet monetization layer.

privates.name: Sila Nanotechnologies
privates.description: Battery materials startup producing silicon-carbon anode material that increases energy density for EVs and grid storage, with manufacturing in Moses Lake, WA.
privates.threat: Silicon-carbon anodes that replace graphite threaten ALB's and MP's position in the battery materials supply chain by reducing lithium requirements per kWh and enabling denser packs that close Tesla's range advantage.

privates.name: Mariana Minerals
privates.description: Software-first vertically integrated critical minerals company using MarianaOS to autonomously operate copper and lithium mines in Utah and Texas.
privates.threat: Autonomous mining operations targeting 50,000 MT/yr copper and first GWh-scale lithium-from-produced-water facility directly threatens MP's rare earth and ALB's lithium market positions with domestically sourced supply.

privates.name: CMBlu Energy
privates.description: German non-lithium battery maker with SolidFlow organic redox technology offering 10+ hour storage without lithium, cobalt, or nickel, with supply agreements with Uniper.
privates.threat: FEOC-compliant non-lithium chemistry with 5 GWh Uniper supply agreement threatens FLNC's and EOSE's market positioning by offering a regulatory-advantaged, critical-mineral-free alternative for European grid storage.

privates.name: Stripe
privates.description: Global payments infrastructure platform processing $1.9T annually, expanding into stablecoins (Bridge), programmable wallets (Privy), and a blockchain for payments (Tempo).
privates.threat: Stripe's $1.9T payment volume and stablecoin/blockchain expansion (Bridge, Tempo) directly challenges V and MA's network fees and positions Stripe as the infrastructure layer for next-generation AI-agent-initiated payments.

privates.name: Revolut
privates.description: UK-based global neobank with 70M+ customers, full banking licenses in UK, EU, Mexico, and Australia, offering payments, crypto, insurance, and business banking.
privates.threat: Revolut's $115B valuation, full banking licenses across 4 jurisdictions, and pending US bank charter threaten PYPL's global digital wallet dominance and V/MA's cross-border fee revenue as it builds a full-stack bank.

privates.name: Ramp
privates.description: AI-powered financial operations platform for corporates covering spend management, corporate cards, procurement, accounting, and AI token spend optimization with $1B+ ARR.
privates.threat: Ramp's corporate card and AI spend management at $44B valuation competes directly with V and MA's commercial card interchange revenue and threatens PYPL's B2B push by automating the entire corporate payment workflow.

privates.name: Figure AI
privates.description: Humanoid robotics company building AI-powered general-purpose robots for commercial and residential deployment, already deployed at BMW manufacturing plants.
privates.threat: Figure's humanoid robots automating labor-intensive workflows threaten fintech-adjacent infrastructure companies like Block/XYZ that depend on human-operated retail and point-of-sale ecosystems.

privates.name: Iambic Therapeutics
privates.description: AI drug discovery company using Enchant platform for translational prediction and generative chemistry to produce clinical-stage small molecules.
privates.threat: Iambic's translational prediction platform targets the same hard-to-drug small molecule space as SDGR, potentially delivering clinical candidates faster and undercutting SDGR's commercial discovery partnerships.

privates.name: Anthropic
privates.description: AI safety company building Claude large language models with industry-leading enterprise penetration through Claude Code (coding), Cowork (agents), and API integrations.
privates.threat: Claude Code's viral adoption and Cowork agent platform threaten MSFT's GitHub Copilot monetization, CRM's Agentforce, and NOW's AI-workflow products by offering a model-layer alternative that bypasses incumbent vendor lock-in.

privates.name: OpenAI
privates.description: Developer of GPT and o-series foundation models powering ChatGPT, Codex, and enterprise APIs, with $110B raised and strategic cloud partnerships with Amazon, NVIDIA, and SoftBank.
privates.threat: OpenAI's Codex and enterprise APIs are embedding at the model layer of MSFT's Azure stack while also competing with MSFT's own Copilot products, creating internal conflicts that threaten CRM, NOW, and SNOW customer relationships.

privates.name: Databricks
privates.description: Data intelligence and AI platform (Lakehouse, Lakebase, Agent Bricks) enabling enterprises to build AI apps and agents on proprietary data, with $1.5B+ Lakebase ARR.
privates.threat: Databricks at $190B has already surpassed SNOW in private market value and its Lakebase-plus-Agent Bricks stack directly displaces SNOW's data cloud and MDB's Atlas for AI-native enterprise workloads.

privates.name: Cognition (Devin)
privates.description: Autonomous AI software engineer (Devin) with $492M ARR and 50% MoM growth serving enterprises including NASA, Goldman Sachs, and Mercedes-Benz.
privates.threat: Devin's autonomous coding with $492M ARR threatens MSFT's GitHub Copilot Enterprise pricing and CRM's developer tools by offering a full-cycle autonomous engineering agent that replaces workflow automation modules.

privates.name: Cohere
privates.description: Enterprise-focused LLM platform (Command, Embed, Rerank) built for secure, private on-premise and cloud deployments with partnerships with Oracle, SAP, Dell, and government agencies.
privates.threat: Cohere's enterprise-grade, air-gapped LLM deployment model challenges MSFT's Azure OpenAI exclusivity and GOOGL's Vertex AI by giving regulated industries (finance, defense, government) a sovereign AI option without cloud hyperscaler dependency.

privates.name: Bridge (Stripe subsidiary)
privates.description: Stablecoin orchestration platform acquired by Stripe for $1.1B, processing $400B+ in stablecoin B2B payments annually and expanding Stripe's crypto payment rails globally.
privates.threat: Bridge's $400B stablecoin volume flowing through Stripe's infrastructure threatens COIN's and CRCL's stablecoin payment ambitions by embedding crypto rails into a $159B payments incumbent that already serves 1.6% of global GDP.

privates.name: Inforcer
privates.description: MSP-focused Microsoft 365 security management platform with Shadow AI detection and real-time threat response, serving SMB clients through managed service providers.
privates.threat: Inforcer's Shadow AI detection and 300% YoY growth in the underserved SMB/MSP market threatens OKTA's identity management and CRWD's Falcon Go product by offering an all-in-one Microsoft 365 security stack at a fraction of the cost.

privates.name: Writer
privates.description: Enterprise generative AI platform for deploying AI agents across business workflows including content creation, customer support, and knowledge management with full data governance.
privates.threat: Writer's enterprise AI agent workflows with Fortune 500 customers like Vanguard and L'Oreal directly compete with CRM's Agentforce and NOW's AI workflow modules by offering model-agnostic agentic automation at lower total cost.

privates.name: Neon (Databricks subsidiary)
privates.description: Serverless Postgres database platform designed for AI agents, enabling instant spin-up of isolated database environments for agentic coding workflows (acquired by Databricks for $1B).
privates.threat: Neon's Lakebase integration into Databricks' Agent Bricks creates a purpose-built agentic database stack that threatens MDB's Atlas and SNOW's Cortex as the default data substrate for AI agent workloads.

privates.name: Klarna
privates.description: Swedish buy-now-pay-later pioneer with 85M+ consumers globally, AI-driven underwriting, and a fully automated customer service model targeting V/MA merchant fees.
privates.threat: Klarna's AI-automated underwriting and checkout network serving 85M consumers directly threatens AFRM's US market share and erodes V/MA merchant discount rates by routing BNPL transactions off traditional card rails.

hf_limits: 13F filings are point-in-time snapshots as of June 30, 2026, filed by Aug 14, 2026. They reflect long U.S. equity positions only; shorts, options (except some reported puts/calls), non-U.S. holdings, and derivatives are not disclosed. Data here is sourced from news articles, last10k.com 13F aggregators, danielscrivner.com, newsquawk.com, and particle.news -- all citing SEC EDGAR filings. SEC EDGAR was used to verify Coatue (CIK 1135730, accession 0000919574-26-005478) and Bridgewater (CIK 1350694, accession 0001350694-26-000003) 13F-HR filings filed 2026-08-14. For many of the 71 universe tickers, no specific hedge-fund-level data was found in available sources; those are marked 'no data'. Institutional aggregate signals (e.g. '48% net buyers of semis') are from a Reuters analysis of 6,371 filers. Dollar values and share counts for Tiger Global and Coatue are sourced from danielscrivner.com which cites the SEC 13F; Bridgewater and Viking from last10k.com which parses SEC filings; Appaloosa from particle.news, newsquawk.com, and Yahoo Finance, all citing SEC filings. No data has been fabricated.
